claims.text: The proposed lubricant is a 2D transition-metal-dichalcogenide HEA nanoflake coating formulated as (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2.
The nanoflake lubricant can be deposited by conventional air spraying.
Air-sprayed (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes will function as a lubricant when deposited on bulk HEA components such as CoCrFeMnNi.
The coating undergoes stress-induced tribocatalytic activity during sliding.
Tribocatalytic transformation of the coating forms a dense, shear-accommodating lubricious glaze.
The resulting glaze is continuous, self-organizing, and composed of adherent nanoflake fragments.
The glaze reduces direct metal-to-metal contact and thereby reduces friction and wear.
The coating can provide low friction and wear at a normal load of approximately 9 N.
The coating will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate on bulk HEAs from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
Relative to untreated HEA surfaces, coating will reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 10–30%.
Relative to untreated HEA surfaces, coating will significantly reduce wear rate.
Prior steel-on-steel testing of the lubricant produced an average coefficient of friction of approximately 0.076 and a wear rate of 2.6 × 10^-9 mm3/(N·m) at 9 N in ambient conditions.
The beneficial effect should persist while coating integrity is maintained and tribocatalytic activity remains operative.
Aggressive oxidation, contaminants, or other extreme conditions that destroy the glaze may limit performance.
The hypothesis will be tested using coated and uncoated HEA controls at room temperature, 400 °C, and 800 °C and at loads of 1, 5, and 9 N.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both friction and wear across all specified conditions, or failure to observe a continuous glaze, will falsify the hypothesis.
